subject: Stellaris AI — true-up discrepancy & proposed settlement
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom@stellaris.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Stellaris AI — true-up discrepancy & proposed settlement

Hi Tom,

Thanks again for the renewal conversation last month. During our post-renewal billing reconciliation we identified a retrospective usage variance that falls outside the committed capacity for Q2 (Apr–Jun 2026). Attached is a line-level CSV (Stellaris_TrueUp_Detail_CSV.xlsx) showing per-day inference hours and the overage calculation.

Summary: 1,420 overage inference hours (net of included committed hours) resulting in a one-time true-up of $21,300 before any credits. The attached spreadsheet breaks this down by model variant and region.

Next steps we propose:
- Confirm the line-level usage (please check the highlighted window: 2026-05-17 to 2026-06-03).
- If you agree, we can issue a one-time invoice and offer a 30-day payment window.
- If you prefer, we can split the charge across two invoices (Aug + Sep) to ease cashflow.

If any of the usage looks like it should be excluded (test traffic, sandbox spikes), flag the specific days and we’ll re-run the audit. Laura is cc’d on this note to handle the accounting side.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
attachments: Stellaris_TrueUp_Detail_CSV.xlsx
From: Tom Reynolds <tom@stellaris.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: finance@stellaris.ai, Ops (Stellaris) <ops@stellaris.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stellaris AI — true-up discrepancy & proposed settlement

Naomi —

Thanks for the detailed breakdown. I pulled this up with our SREs and we see two short-lived spikes that coincide with a load test we accidentally pointed at prod on 2026-05-19 and another misconfigured job on 2026-05-28 that retried several times. We certainly expect to be accountable for genuine production consumption but would like those two windows excluded or at least reviewed.

Can you confirm the exact timestamps you used for sampling? I’m attaching our internal incident export for those dates (excerpted) — you should see the spike tied to deployment IDs.

If the numbers remain after reconciling, we’ll need an amortization option: splitting across Aug and Sep would be preferred. Also asking the team if we can trade a portion of the overage for an increased committed band — we’re evaluating a ~15% uplift for next term.

—Tom
Tom Reynolds
VP Engineering, Stellaris AI
tom@stellaris.ai
attachments: stellaris_incident_export_excerpt.txt
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom@stellaris.ai>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stellaris AI — true-up discrepancy & proposed settlement

Hi Tom —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the incident export. Laura — can your team reconcile the spike windows vs. our usage logs and confirm whether those days were attributable to non-billable test traffic? If we confirm they were internal test errors, we’ll exclude them from the true-up.

Ben — looping you in from Sales because Tom mentioned a possible uplift to committed capacity (~15%). If Stellaris is ready to increase the committed band, we can offer one of two settlement paths:

Path A — Exclude confirmed test-window usage; invoice remaining true-up in full (30-day term).
Path B — Split the remaining true-up across two invoices (Aug + Sep) and apply a 10% settlement credit if Stellaris signs a 12-month +15% capacity increase starting at the next term. The credit is applied to the one-time true-up only (not the new committed rate).

Next steps:
- Laura to validate the two spike windows by EOD tomorrow.
- Tom to confirm whether Stellaris is comfortable with Path A or Path B (or propose an alternative).

Thanks,
Naomi
Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
attachments: none
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom@stellaris.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stellaris AI — true-up discrepancy & proposed settlement

Tom —

Thanks for the context. Happy to work with you on a pragmatic settlement. To make this straightforward: we can offer Path B with the following commercial tweak — a 10% settlement credit on the residual true-up if Stellaris executes the proposed +15% commit for 12 months by Aug 15. We’ll memorialize the uplift in an amendment and include a clause to ensure the committed capacity is effective at the start of the next billing cycle.

Operationally we’ll:
- Reissue an adjusted settlement PDF reflecting the excluded windows (assuming Laura confirms) and the split-payment schedule.
- If you sign by Aug 15, credit will be applied to the one-time settlement and we’ll add the amended commit to your subscription.

If you need net-30 instead of net-45 for the first installment, we can accommodate that on a case-by-case basis.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Tom Reynolds <tom@stellaris.ai>

Subject: Re: Stellaris AI — true-up discrepancy & proposed settlement

Ben / Naomi —

Appreciate the flexibility. We’re aligned to Path B contingent on Laura’s reconciliation. We’ll commit to the +15% capacity for 12 months and will target Aug 12 to sign the amendment so the credit applies. Please send the updated settlement PDF and a DocuSign link for the amendment. Also confirm the two excluded dates (05/19 and 05/28) once Laura confirms.

Tom
